This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz. protoemu targets 60 MHz: 16.6 ns.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
Configuration docs: https://librelane.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/configuration.html

protoemu changes one template value below (FP_PDN_VPITCH) and adds the SRAM block at the end,
which also turns Magic DRC off. Each change says why.
Save some time
protoemu: KLayout DRC stays off in the flow on purpose. The precheck job runs the same CMOS5L deck on
the same GDS (16 minutes on the empty template), so DRC sign-off is the precheck's. Set it to 1 to get
the report in the GDS job too, as Ken Pettit's local flow does.
Don't put clock buffers on the outputs
Reduce wasted space
Absolute die size
protoemu: the template's 50 um pitch becomes 44.96 um, four times the SRAM's 11.24 um supply-column pitch,
so with FP_PDN_VOFFSET and FP_PDN_VSPACING below a VPWR/VGND pair lands on the SRAM's columns (Pettit).
Clock
Don't generate power rings
MAGIC_DEF_LABELS may cause issues with LVS
Only export pin area in LEF (without any connected nets)
//sram: ---- protoemu: two IHP RM_IHPSG13_1P_512x32_c2_bm_bist SRAMs (core.table_ram.ram_a and ram_b in the netlist) ----
//sram_source: Taken from Ken Pettit's ihp-um-janestreet-prism (src/config.json, main 2026-10-15), whose two 512x32 SRAMs pass precheck in the same orientations and on the same stripe grid, and his walkthrough https://kdp1965.github.io/ihp-um-janestreet-prism/ihp_sram_macro.html. protoemu moves the pair 5 grid pitches right and spreads it to the core's top and bottom (see //macros). Values checked against the macro's LEF at IHP-Open-PDK 89d42ee6d2fd, the commit Tiny Tapeout's flow installs.
//meta: The Classic flow plus two steps from librelane_plugin_protoemu/ (found because LibreLane runs from the repo root): after the PDN generator, full-height stripes over each SRAM's Metal4 supply columns; after the post-CTS resizer, an antenna diode on each SRAM input pin (see //antenna).
//macros: Views from the PDK (sg13cmos5l_sram links to sg13g2_sram). The flow's corner names map onto IHP's: the fast lib is characterised at -55 C, not -40 C. 'vh' is a ports-only black box for Verilator lint and Yosys. Locations are the lower-left corners in um. ram_a is flipped (FS) so its pin edge faces up and ram_b's (N) faces down: their address and data pins look at each other across the channel where the table logic goes. Both pin edges are on Metal2, and Metal3 is the tile's only horizontal routing layer (Metal2 and Metal4 run vertically, TopMetal1 is the harness's), so every wire between the channel and the rest of the chip leaves through the channel's open ends on Metal3. Pettit's spots, flush left at x 3.36 with a 145 um channel, left one open end: 345 Metal3 tracks for this design's 244 crossing nets, and the first layout build (GitHub run 44047118911) routed 25 nets straight over the SRAMs and ended with 382 shorts. Here x = 228.16 = 3.36 + 5 x 44.96 opens both ends and keeps each SRAM column exactly where it was against the stripe grid; ram_a sits on the core's bottom edge and ram_b's top is 1.44 um under its top edge, so the channel is 318.96 um tall (759 Metal3 tracks at each end); ram_b's pin edge is on a row boundary, as Pettit's is; and the left 223 um of rows, under the tile's pins (x 29.6-191.2), have no macro above them.
//halo: Standard cells keep 2 um from the SRAM's sides (NWell spacing at its edge) and 0.48 um from its top and bottom (Pettit).
//obstructions: No signal routing over the SRAMs on Metal2 to Metal4, except a 2.6 um band at each pin edge (ram_a's top at y 195.12, ram_b's bottom at y 514.08). The LEF already obstructs most of it; this also keeps the router off the Metal4 supply columns (Pettit).
//pdn: The tile grid is vertical Metal4 only. Width 2.1 + spacing 3.52 = 5.62 um, the SRAM's VDD!-to-VSS! column pitch; offset 6.15 centres the first VPWR stripe at 9.03 um (Pettit). pdn_cfg.tcl is LibreLane's without the per-macro grid, which fails on a one-layer grid (PDN-0233).
//pdn_macro: The SRAM has two supplies on VPWR (VDD! for its periphery, VDDARRAY! for the bit cells) and VSS! on VGND, so each instance gets two lines.
//pdn_check: pdngen's grid check runs before Protoemu.ExtendPowerStripes connects the SRAM columns, so it reports them; LVS and the IR drop report are the verdict (Pettit).
//stripes: Protoemu.ExtendPowerStripes: each grid stripe crossing an SRAM moves onto its nearest free supply column of the same polarity, each region of the macro gets whole pairs, and each bit-cell array gets a pair on every other column pair. The tile's signal pins are placed after this step, so it cannot steer around them; with the SRAMs at x 228.16-644.8 no column stripe runs under them, and the grid's own stripes stop at the core edge (y 706.86), 2.8 um below the pins, as in the template. This is the setting Pettit's submission signed off with.
//drc: protoemu changes the template here. Magic DRC is off: it took 44 of the empty template's 50 GDS minutes, and it judges the SRAM from its abstract (Pettit turned it off for that reason). The precheck's KLayout CMOS5L deck is the DRC sign-off.
//overlap: Magic's extraction sees the SRAM LEF's Metal4 obstruction bar at the VDD!/VDDARRAY! break (LEF y 39.1-45.2) under every stripe that bridges the two; the GDS has no metal there and both pins are VPWR. Pettit counted 22 such overlaps with clean KLayout DRC and LVS, and waived the check.
//antenna: Protoemu.DiodesOnSramPins puts one diode beside each of the 156 input pins of each SRAM, as Pettit's flow does; the flow's rule-based repair (RUN_ANTENNA_REPAIR) still covers every other net. The SRAM LEF carries antenna data on every input, but Pettit found the rule-based repair did not always protect the nets driving the macro, and calls the diodes cheap insurance. The step reads DIODE_CELL as cell/pin, LibreLane's documented format; the PDK default lacks the pin.
